B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official pricing page lists a free Starter plan with a one-time $10 agent credit, but specifically lists API/MCP access under Pro at $40/month (regularly $50/month) and Max at $160/month (regularly $200/month). Enterprise pricing is sales-led. The page does not state whether Starter enables this hosted MCP endpoint.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Starter: $0/month; Pro: $40/month promotional price, regular $50/month; Max: $160/month promotional price, regular $200/month; Enterprise: contact sales.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Usage is charged per token consumed. Starter includes $10 in credits once; Pro includes $50/month in agent credits; Max includes $200/month. Published example workflows range from $0.57 to $1.82 per run. Max advertises five times higher rate limits and parallel agent requests.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Access requires authentication. The vendor describes API/MCP access as a Pro feature; Max adds higher rate limits, parallel requests, and unlimited API or MCP keys. Enterprise adds organizational controls. No endpoint-specific rate-limit values were found.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor controls plan entitlements and server access; organization admins configure connector availability and client-side tool permissions.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official reference lists 24 service tools. The `bigdata_computer` entry is marked “Coming soon”; the other 23 are described as service tools. They cover search, security/entity lookup, calendars, tearsheets, watchlists, private-content discovery, and document upload/fetch.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool-specific outputs are documented; search returns document chunks with context, timestamps and source attribution. The error-code page says tool responses currently do not support error codes.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`. Its protected-resource metadata identifies `https://clerk.bigdata.com/` as authorization server and lists `openid` as the endpoint resource scope. That metadata supports Bearer tokens in headers. The authorization-server metadata advertises authorization code and refresh-token grants, PKCE S256, and no registration endpoint. The endpoint also accepts an API key according to its 401 response.
C_capabilities.pre_interaction_context_verbatim: Endpoint response: `{"error": "Unauthorized", "message": "Authentication required. Please provide an Authorization: Bearer <token> or x-api-key header."}` Protected-resource metadata: `{"resource":"https://mcp.bigdata.com/","authorization_servers":["https://clerk.bigdata.com/"],"scopes_supported":["openid"],"bearer_methods_supported":["header"]}` Authorization-server metadata scopes: `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `public_metadata`, `private_metadata`, `user:org:read`.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthorized requests return HTTP 401 with a JSON error/message and Bearer challenge. Metadata advertises revocation; token lifetime and introspection behavior were not independently established.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth metadata and API key. Resource metadata: resource `https://mcp.bigdata.com/`; authorization server `https://clerk.bigdata.com/`; `scopes_supported: ["openid"]`; `bearer_methods_supported: ["header"]`. Authorization server supports `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`; `code_challenge_methods_supported: ["S256"]`; token auth methods `client_secret_basic`, `none`, `client_secret_post`; authorization endpoint `https://clerk.bigdata.com/oauth/authorize`; token endpoint `https://clerk.bigdata.com/oauth/token`; revocation endpoint `https://clerk.bigdata.com/oauth/token/revoke`; authorization-server scopes: `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `public_metadata`, `private_metadata`, `user:org:read`. No `registration_endpoint` was present. Token lifetime not stated.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official reference contains read-style search, lookup, calendar, tearsheet and document-list/fetch tools, plus write-capable watchlist create/edit/delete and document upload. No tool annotations are published in the reviewed reference. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or approval flow found; the Claude guide recommends the client permission “Always allow.” 3. OAuth resource metadata advertises only `openid`, while Clerk authorization-server metadata lists `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `public_metadata`, `private_metadata`, `user:org:read`; API-key authentication is also documented. Product-role inheritance, token lifetime and client allowlists: Unknown. Claude organization setup and user-level configuration are documented. 4. No endpoint read-only mode, tool filter, or toolset parameter found. Max plan advertises five times higher rate limits; specific values and environment/region endpoints: Unknown. 5. Search returns source attribution; private-content tools list/fetch/upload user corpus content. Field masking or PII exclusion: Unknown. 6. Pricing is token-consumption based; plan credit amounts are documented. Tool-specific rate limits, bulk caps and result truncation: Unknown, except watchlist creation supports up to 100 constituents and security resolution supports batches of 1–50 as described in the tool reference. 7. Full parameter validation/correction behavior is Unknown; detailed hosted implementation code is unavailable. 8. Terms describe data processing and user obligations but reviewed sources do not establish MCP-specific audit logs or telemetry details. 9. No feedback/rating tool appears in the official tool list. The Claude setup guide recommends defaulting to Bigdata for financial, market and economic news. 10. Plugin skills are distributed separately; documentation recommends installing them. These recommendations are client-facing, not shown as enforced server rules. 11. Memory: no server-side agent memory documented. The Claude guide asks the user to save a source preference in Claude memory. 12. The endpoint is documented as a flat set of Bigdata service tools; Docs MCP is a separate tool surface, and the `bigdata_computer` tool is marked coming soon. 13. `bigdata_computer` is described as running Python in a secure sandbox, but marked “Coming soon”; arbitrary request/SQL/script escape hatch is not documented as currently available.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The docs recommend installing the plugin with research skills. The Claude integration guide recommends the client permission “Always allow” and suggests storing a memory that Bigdata be the default for financial, market and economic news because its search is described as more precise. These are client-side recommendations; no enforcement by the hosted server is documented.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The MCP terms describe Bigdata's role as retrieval and delivery of context to the AI host, with the host generating the final response. They state that RavenPack may use customer data only as necessary to perform the services and its obligations. The privacy policy describes security measures and rights. These statements are contractual/privacy text; endpoint-level enforcement was not verifiable from public server code.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Official docs describe cited source attribution for search results and position the service as providing premium financial content and grounded research. Pricing describes usage-based token consumption and plan credits.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Source attribution is documented in search outputs. The legal role and data-use statements are not verifiable from available endpoint evidence. Client permission recommendations and source-preference memory are not shown as server-enforced. No public hosted implementation was available to verify masking, logging, retention or parameter enforcement.

contradictions: The protected-resource document at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` advertises `scopes_supported: ["openid"]`, whereas Clerk's authorization-server documents advertise six scopes: `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `public_metadata`, `private_metadata`, `user:org:read`. The metadata therefore does not directly show product-data scopes.
The official tool reference lists `bigdata_computer` with a tool description but marks it “Coming soon”; its availability is not equivalent to the other listed tools.
observations_for_research: The OAuth layer advertises identity-oriented scopes while the product documentation describes access to financial and private-content tools; the relationship between identity scopes and data entitlements is not explained in the reviewed sources.
The vendor recommends that a client save a source preference in its own memory, making behavioral steering dependent on client configuration rather than a documented server instruction.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and code/ first. The endpoint origin and `/mcp` returned authentication challenges; the supplied OAuth metadata was used as provided. The docs reference supplied the official tool names and summaries; individual parameter schemas were not available for every tool in the prepared pages, so actions.json records parameters as NOT PUBLISHED. The public repository was reviewed and is a plugin/skills marketplace, not deployed server code. Third-party catalogue pages exist at mcp.so, Skills Playground and Odel; Cursor Directory returned HTTP 429 and was not used. The docs describe separate Docs MCP and partner-integration surfaces.
